prologue.title: A Normal Morning
prologue.narrator: The ends of the world rarely begin with a loud noise. Sometimes they begin with a cup of coffee.
prologue.text:
You wake up with pale morning light on the wall.

The city outside is already living its ordinary little life.

Your phone buzzes.

Message from Nora:

> Coffee in twenty minutes?
> I'll pay if you promise not to talk about your dead plants yet.

Nora.

Your friend for long enough to know your silences.
Too close to lie convincingly.
Too stubborn to admit when she's scared.

On the radio, a voice talks about international tensions.

You only half listen.

Like everyone else.

choices.text: Tell her you're on your way
Reply to Nora with a joke

radio_matin.title: The Morning Radio
radio_matin.narrator: Bad news often sounds less serious when it is read calmly.
radio_matin.text:
You turn up the volume.

> Authorities are calling for calm.
> No immediate danger has been reported.
> Civil defense drills scheduled for today will go ahead as planned.

Then a cereal ad cuts off the broadcast.

Your phone buzzes again.

Nora:

> Did you fall back asleep?
> If so, I'm keeping your croissant.

You grab your keys.

cafe_blague.title: The Café of Small Habits
cafe_blague.narrator: It is often the tiny habits that make the world feel solid.
cafe_blague.text:
On the way, you text Nora.

> My plants aren't dead.
> They're just pretending, to get attention.

She replies in three seconds:

> Like you.

When you reach the café, she's already there.

Hair tied up any old way.
Oversized military jacket.
The smile of someone who has decided to laugh at the world before it can laugh at her.

She raises your croissant.

**"I nearly ate it. I was heroic."**

For a few minutes, everything is simple.

Hot coffee.
Fine rain.
Nora grumbling about the spoon being too small.

On TV, politicians clench their jaws.

Nobody really watches.

choices.text: Suggest stopping by the covered market
Ask Nora if she looks tired

cafe_simple.title: The Café, That Morning
cafe_simple.narrator: It is often the tiny habits that make the world feel solid.
cafe_simple.text:
When you arrive at the café, Nora is already there.

She's ordered for you.

**"I got the usual. If you've changed your taste overnight, too bad for you."**

Rain draws lines on the window.

On TV, a red banner slides along the bottom of the screen.

> MAJOR TENSIONS — AUTHORITIES CALL FOR CALM

Nora follows your gaze.

For a second, her smile cracks.

Then she shrugs.

**"They always call for calm when they've run out of things to say."**

choices.text: Suggest a short walk before going home

nora_fatigue.title: Nora's Dark Circles
nora_fatigue.narrator: Some people hide secrets better than they hide exhaustion.
nora_fatigue.text:
You notice her dark circles.

Not just from one bad night.

From several.

Nora turns her cup between her hands.

**"I worked late."**

You know she works at a research center near the old military hospital.

On her wrist, a small bandage peeks out from her sleeve.

When she sees you looking, she pulls the fabric down.

Too fast.

**"Don't make that face. It's nothing. Medical tests for work."**

Then she smiles.

Not her real smile.

**"Want to walk a bit? I need some air."**

choices.text: Ask how her family is doing

indice_pansement.title: The Bandage
indice_pansement.narrator: Important clues know how to disguise themselves as ordinary details.
indice_pansement.text:
You ask her if everything is all right.

Nora glances down at her wrist.

**"They asked me to redo some tests. Nothing dramatic."**

She tries to laugh.

**"Apparently I'm compatible with far too many machines."**

The sentence is strange.

She seems to regret saying it.

Before you can ask what she means, the café lights flicker.

One second.

Then everything comes back.

choices.text: Step outside for some air with Nora

tv_cafe.title: The Silent Television
tv_cafe.narrator: Screens sometimes announce the end of the world before the world agrees to hear it.
tv_cafe.text:
You look at the television.

The sound is off, but the pictures are enough.

Maps.
Arrows.
Closed faces.
A news anchor touching his earpiece as if someone had just told him not to panic.

Nora is watching too.

She murmurs:

**"Not today..."**

You turn toward her.

She pretends she hasn't spoken.

At the same moment, everyone in the café gets a notification.

A short sound.

Identical.

journee_normale.title: The City Before
journee_normale.narrator: Before the panic, there is always a last moment when everything could have stayed normal.
journee_normale.text:
You walk through the fine rain.

Nora talks about pointless things.

The café's new owner.
A dog that always barks at 7:12 AM.
Vending machines now selling triangular sandwiches that are far too confident.

You laugh.

So does she.

Then she stops in front of a bookshop.

In the window, a children's book shows a rocket.

Nora rests her hand on the glass.

**"When I was little, I thought fallout shelters were rockets turned upside down. You went underground to leave for somewhere else."**

She takes her hand back.

**"It's silly."**

But her voice is not silly at all.

choices.text: Ask her why she is thinking about shelters

librairie.title: The Bookshop
librairie.narrator: Some places seem built to survive catastrophes, even when they cannot.
librairie.text:
The bookshop smells of paper, dust, and old heating.

An elderly man sorts books by size.

Nora picks up a poetry collection.

**"If the world ends, I hope it will have the courtesy to let me finish this page."**

The bookseller smiles.

**"The world has never been very polite."**

The shop radio crackles.

The music cuts out.

A deep beep sounds.

nora_sait.title: What Nora Isn't Saying
nora_sait.narrator: The silence of someone you know can make more noise than a siren.
nora_sait.text:
You ask what she knows.

Nora opens her mouth.

Closes it.

Her phone buzzes.

She reads.

Her face changes.

Not surprise.

Fear.

But not surprise.

**"We have to leave. Now."**

At that moment, the sirens start.

They don't sound like the drills.

They're longer.

Lower.

Older.

alerte.title: The Alert
alerte.narrator: Some sounds split a life in two: before, and after.
alerte.text:
Every phone shrieks at once.

> NATIONAL EMERGENCY
> PROBABLE STRATEGIC IMPACTS
> REPORT TO A SHELTER IMMEDIATELY
> ESTIMATED TIME: 18 MINUTES

The café falls silent.

Then someone laughs.

A short, disbelieving laugh.

Then a cup falls.

Then the city erupts into motion.

Nora grabs your arm.

**"We don't have eighteen minutes. They always understate it to avoid riots."**

explication_interrompue.title: Not Now
explication_interrompue.narrator: Some questions the world refuses to wait for.
explication_interrompue.text:
You hold Nora back.

**"What do you know?"**

She clenches her teeth.

**"Not now."**

**"Nora."**

She looks at you.

**"If I explain, you'll want to do exactly what they expect of you. And I can't let you do that."**

Before you can understand, a distant explosion makes the shop windows shake.

Nora tugs you by the sleeve.

choices.text: Refuse to move without an answer

aider_cafe.title: The First Seconds
aider_cafe.narrator: Humanity sometimes begins by picking up someone who has fallen.
aider_cafe.text:
A waitress has cut herself on a broken cup.

A man stands frozen in front of the television.

You help the waitress to her feet.

Nora wants to leave.

You see her anger.

Then her face changes.

She grabs napkins.

She knows what to do.

Too well.

The waitress whispers thank you.

Nora just glances at the time on her phone.

14 minutes.

appel.title: The Call
appel.narrator: In disasters, phones become bridges that are far too fragile.
appel.text:
You call.

The line rings.

Once.

Twice.

Nora tugs at your sleeve.

**"We have to go."**

The line connects.

A familiar voice says your name.

But behind it, you hear the sirens.

The same sound.

You don't have enough words to say everything.

choices.text: Just tell them you love them
Try to explain what to do

rue_panique.title: The City Running
rue_panique.narrator: When everyone flees at once, the city becomes a wounded organism.
rue_panique.text:
The streets are packed.

Cars stuck in traffic.
Horns blaring nonstop.
People running with bags too heavy to carry.
Parents carrying children in pajamas.

A billboard keeps selling seaside holidays.

Nora knows a route through the old service galleries beneath the hospital.

**"There's a military shelter under the complex. If they've opened it, we can get in."**

A child cries beside an overturned car.

Farther on, a soldier shouts that the bridge is closed.

enfant_voiture.title: The Overturned Car
enfant_voiture.narrator: Saving someone sometimes takes exactly the time you don't have.
enfant_voiture.text:
The child is trapped in the back seat.

His mother tries to open the door.

Nora swears, then helps you pull.

The door resists.

A plane passes overhead.

This time, lower.

You pull again.

The door finally gives way.

The mother clutches her child to her chest.

But you've lost time.

Far too much.

In the street, the people who were running toward the galleries have already vanished.

Nora looks into the distance.

Then she looks at you as if you had just hurt her.

**"That's why I can't let you choose."**

Her voice trembles.

**"Because you'll always choose others before yourself."**

Another tremor runs through the buildings.

This time, the windows explode at the far end of the avenue.

choices.text: Keep going toward the galleries anyway
Tell Nora the child was meant to live

soldat.title: The Checkpoint
soldat.narrator: Order sometimes holds only because no one has yet shouted loudly enough.
soldat.text:
The soldier is young.

Too young.

He repeats:

**"The bridge is closed. Report to the designated shelters."**

Nora keeps her head down.

The soldier looks at you.

Then he looks at Nora.

His expression changes.

Recognition.

Not of Nora.

Of you.

He reaches for his radio.

Nora sees it.

She shoves you into the crowd.

**"Now."**

nora_fissure.title: The Crack
nora_fissure.narrator: Under the panic, some secrets begin to breathe.
nora_fissure.text:
You ask what she means.

Nora clenches her fists.

**"You always help. Even when it destroys you."**

**"Is that supposed to be a flaw?"**

She laughs without joy.

**"Today, yes."**

A military announcement crackles:

> All citizens must report to the shelters.
> Medical priority for compatible subjects.

Nora goes pale.

Compatible subject.

Two words that shouldn't have mattered.

But they do.

choices.text: Ask her if this concerns you

arrestation.title: The Wrong Look
arrestation.narrator: Being important is rarely good news when soldiers are running toward you.
arrestation.text:
You stay a second too long.

The soldier speaks into his radio.

**"I think I've found him."**

Nora grabs your arm, but two soldiers are already turning around.

They don't shout your name.

They say a code.

**"Subject S-12 in sight."**

Nora strikes the soldier with a violence that shocks you.

Not a heroine.

Someone who refuses to lose.

She drags you into the crowd.

galeries.title: The Service Galleries
galeries.narrator: Beneath cities, secrets often have tired neon lights.
galeries.text:
Nora opens a metal door behind the old hospital.

You don't ask how she knows the code.

She types it in far too fast.

The galleries smell of dust, disinfectant, and warm electricity.

On the wall, arrows point:

> SHELTER B-7
> HEMATOLOGY LAB
> RESTRICTED ACCESS

You stop at the word hematology.

Nora gently pushes you.

**"Not that way."**

But her voice says the opposite.

choices.text: Ask why she knows the code

question_code.title: The Code
question_code.narrator: The most fragile lies are the ones told too quickly.
question_code.text:
**"Why do you know the code?"**

Nora keeps walking.

**"I worked here."**

**"You told me 'near here.' Not here."**

She doesn't answer right away.

**"There are a lot of things I told you wrong."**

**"And what matters?"**

She stops.

The sirens vibrate through the walls.

**"That you stay alive."**

laboratoire_indice.title: The Forbidden Corridor
laboratoire_indice.narrator: A word on a door can hold an entire life.
laboratoire_indice.text:
Files have been left abandoned on a cart.

Nora says your name.

Not loudly.

But with immense fear.

You grab the first file.

Your name is on it.

Or rather:

> Subject S-12
> Exceptional serum response
> Post-radiological compatibility: 98.7%

Your blood.

The world sways.

Nora rips the file out of your hands.

**"Not like this. You weren't supposed to learn it like this."**

A distant explosion cuts the lights.

They come back red.

choices.text: Put it off for later and run

premiere_verite.title: What You Are
premiere_verite.narrator: Some truths save no one when they arrive too late.
premiere_verite.text:
Nora closes her eyes.

**"Your blood resists."**

She speaks quickly.

**"Particles. Radiation. Whatever comes after. They found it after the accident last winter, when you gave blood. They put me on the project because I knew you."**

**"With enough samples, they can make a serum. Not for everyone. Not right away. But enough to rebuild something."**

You feel the cold arrive before the rest.

**"And the samples?"**

Nora looks at you.

**"They would kill you."**

choices.text: Run toward the shelter to understand
Ask why she lied to you

nora_aveu_partiel.title: The Lie
nora_aveu_partiel.narrator: A lie can be a prison built out of love.
nora_aveu_partiel.text:
**"Why didn't you tell me?"**

Nora trembles.

**"Because I knew what you'd do."**

**"You would have agreed. Maybe not right away. But you would have ended up agreeing. Because there would have been children, sick people, people crying on television. And you... you would have said yes."**

She wipes her eyes angrily.

**"So I stole the data. I delayed the protocol. I sabotaged their access."**

Then, lower:

**"I may have condemned thousands of people before the bombs even fell. But you were still breathing."**

abri_entree.title: Shelter B-7
abri_entree.narrator: Survival sometimes takes the form of a door that won't open for everyone.
abri_entree.text:
The door to shelter B-7 is enormous.

Dozens of people are waiting outside.

A system repeats:

> LIMITED CAPACITY
> PRIORITY TO ESSENTIAL PERSONNEL
> PRIORITY TO MEDICAL PROFILES

The crowd screams.

A military doctor tries to keep order.

When he sees you, his face freezes.

He murmurs:

**"It's him."**

Nora steps in front of you.

**"No."**

A rumble passes through the city above.

The first impact has landed.

Not here.

Not yet.

medecin_revele.title: Protocol S-12
medecin_revele.narrator: People who want to save the world rarely speak like monsters.
medecin_revele.text:
The doctor raises his hands.

He doesn't look cruel.

Only exhausted.

**"Your blood contains an immune response we don't know how to reproduce. The serum can save people exposed to fallout. Not everyone. But enough."**

Nora shouts:

**"Don't listen to him."**

The doctor continues.

**"Full extraction is necessary. It will be lethal."**

The crowd hears enough.

Faces turn toward you.

No hatred.

Worse.

Hope.

Nora backs toward a side door.

**"Come with me. Now."**

choices.text: Ask how many lives are at stake

combien.title: How Many Lives?
combien.narrator: Numbers are sometimes more unbearable than screams.
combien.text:
You ask how many.

The doctor doesn't look away.

**"In this shelter? Three hundred and twelve. In the other sectors, if we transmit the formula in time: several thousand. Perhaps more."**

Nora whispers:

**"He says perhaps."**

The doctor answers gently:

**"Yes. Perhaps. That's all the world has left."**

Nora looks at you.

**"And I'm telling you for certain. You're going to die for certain."**

The ceiling trembles.

Dust falls like gray snow.

triage.title: Triage
triage.narrator: Helping everyone is sometimes a way of not choosing yet.
triage.text:
You help civilians come inside.

An elderly woman.
Two children.
An injured man.
The café waitress, still pale.

Nora helps you despite herself.

She knows how to organize an evacuation.

Too well.

The doctor watches you from the inner doorway.

He doesn't rush you.

That's worse.

He waits for you to understand.

Nora rests a hand on your shoulder.

**"We've helped enough. Now I'm saving you."**

choices.text: Keep triaging until the last civilian

nora_fuite.title: The Side Door
nora_fuite.narrator: When someone loves you too fiercely, it can look like running away.
nora_fuite.text:
Nora pulls you through a side door.

Behind you, voices rise.

The doctor shouts your name.

The door closes.

Nora locks it manually.

**"There's an old maintenance shuttle. It leads to the southern tunnels. If we leave now, we can get out before the secondary blast."**

**"And the others?"**

She closes her eyes.

**"The others aren't you."**

The sentence falls between you.

Monstrous.

Sincere.

Impossible to forget.

choices.text: Tell her you can't do this

confrontation.title: What the World Is Worth
confrontation.narrator: There is no clean enough sentence for weighing one life against all the others.
confrontation.text:
**"I can't let these people die."**

Nora looks at you as if you've just confirmed an old fear.

**"I know."**

She laughs without joy.

**"That's exactly why I lied."**

**"You had no right."**

**"No."**

She doesn't defend herself.

**"But I did it anyway."**

An automated voice announces:

> ESTIMATED MAIN IMPACT: 04 MINUTES
> SHELTER B-7 — FINAL SEALING IMMINENT

Nora rests her forehead against yours.

**"I don't want to be forgiven. I want you to live."**

choices.text: Go back to the extraction room

salle_extraction.title: The White Room
salle_extraction.narrator: Saving the world can mean a room too clean, with a single chair in the middle.
salle_extraction.text:
The extraction room is white.

Too white.

A medical chair waits for you.

Cables.
Sterile bags.
Machines already set up.

The doctor speaks softly.

**"We can start the protocol. You'll lose consciousness quickly. You won't suffer for long."**

Nora arrives behind you.

Her face is ravaged.

**"No."**

The doctor doesn't look at her.

**"He has to choose."**

The automated voice announces:

> ESTIMATED MAIN IMPACT: 03 MINUTES

Everything narrows down to you.

To Nora.

To the chair.

To the lives no one can see.

tunnel_final.title: The Southern Tunnels
tunnel_final.narrator: Running away is not always cowardice. Sometimes it is simply choosing whom you refuse to lose.
tunnel_final.text:
You run through the southern tunnels.

The city trembles above.

Nora knows every junction.

She has prepared this.

You understand it now.

Not since this morning.

Since weeks ago.

She had planned a way to take you away from the lab.

A way to keep you alive.

Even if the world needed you.

At the end of the tunnel, a door opens onto the outside.

Behind you, the loudspeakers repeat:

> PROTOCOL S-12 NOT LAUNCHED
> ESTIMATED LOSSES: CRITICAL

Nora doesn't look back.

**"Hate me later. Live now."**

troisieme_voie.title: The Third Way
troisieme_voie.narrator: Hope is sometimes the last lie we tell ourselves before we choose.
troisieme_voie.text:
You ask for another solution.

The doctor speaks fast.

**"A partial extraction won't be enough."**

Nora clings to that sentence.

**"But it could help?"**

**"Too little. Too late. Maybe a few dozen. Maybe no one."**

The voice announces:

> ESTIMATED MAIN IMPACT: 02 MINUTES

The world doesn't give you a third way.

Only a slower way of refusing to choose.

choix_sacrifice.title: The World
choix_sacrifice.narrator: Some choices save lives and destroy the one who was watching you.
choix_sacrifice.text:
You sit in the chair.

Nora almost stops breathing.

**"No."**

You want to tell her something perfect.

But there's nothing.

So you only say:

**"I'm sorry."**

She shakes her head.

Tears fall, silent.

**"Me too."**

The doctor starts the protocol.

Behind the glass, people no longer scream.

The first sample fills with an almost luminous red.

Nora presses her hand against the glass.

You press yours against it, facing hers.

The light outside turns white.

choices.text: Give up and leave with Nora

choix_nora.title: Nora
choix_nora.narrator: Saving one person can sometimes mean leaving the world to its silence.
choix_nora.text:
You choose Nora.

Or maybe she chooses for you.

Maybe there's no difference anymore.

You reach the tunnel exit.

The city is behind you.

The sirens have grown distant.

The sky opens in a white flash above Saint-Oriel.

Nora pulls you against her.

Not to protect you.

She knows she can't.

Just so you're not alone.

The blast arrives later than expected.

Late enough for her to say:

**"I know you may never forgive me. But you're alive."**

fin_partielle.title: A Few Lives
fin_partielle.narrator: Compromises sometimes taste of blood and of not being enough.
fin_partielle.text:
You refuse the full protocol.

But you accept the partial extraction.

The doctor knows it isn't enough.

Nora knows it's too much.

The machine takes your blood.

Not all of it.

Enough to make you waver.

Not enough to save the world.

Later, people will say the partial serum saved twenty-seven people.

Or thirty.

Or twelve.

The numbers will change depending on who tells the story.

Nora stays close to you.

You survive.

So does she.

But between you there will always be this question:

how many lives is half a measure of courage worth?

fin_sacrifice.title: Ending — The Serum
fin_sacrifice.narrator: The world does not always remember correctly those who save it.
fin_sacrifice.text:
The first doses come out before dawn.

Then more.

Protocol S-12 does not save everyone.

No honest story ends like this.

But it saves enough lives for children to breathe in shelters.
Enough for doctors to keep going.
Enough for someone to still speak of the future.

Nora survives.

She refuses ceremonies.

She keeps only a photo of the two of you at the café.

On the back, she writes:

> You would have hated for anyone to call this a miracle.

Years later, when the first flowers grow back on the rooftops of Saint-Oriel, some say the world was saved by a serum.

Nora knows the world was saved by someone who didn't have enough time to say goodbye.

fin_nora.title: Ending — Two Survivors
fin_nora.narrator: There are worlds we don't save, only people we refuse to lose.
fin_nora.text:
You survive.

Not easily.

Not cleanly.

The world doesn't end in a single light.

It goes on, wounded.

Cities fall.
Shelters go dark.
Radio messages call for help for weeks.

Nora barely sleeps anymore.

Neither do you.

Sometimes she looks at you as if she is still checking that her crime is breathing.

You want to hate her.

Some days, you manage it.

Other days, you remember her hand in yours.

One evening, far from Saint-Oriel, she asks:

**"If it had to be done again... would you still let me save you?"**

You don't have an answer big enough.

Only silence.

And she stays anyway.

fin_trop_tard.title: Ending — Not Choosing
fin_trop_tard.narrator: Sometimes not choosing is still a choice. But it is not always the most human one.
fin_trop_tard.text:
You stay.

One second.

Then another.

There must have been a good reason.

To understand better.
To find the right words.
To not abandon anyone.
To not make a mistake.

But this time, your hesitation saves no one.

Not the child.
Not Nora.
Not the people in the shelter.
Not you.

The light arrives without a sound.

For an instant, everything turns white.

Then there are no more sirens.

No more questions.

No more choices.

Only the time you still thought you had.

retard_enfant.title: Lost Time
retard_enfant.narrator: Saving someone sometimes takes exactly the time you didn't have.
retard_enfant.text:
You run toward the old hospital.

But the street is no longer the same.

The military has closed the passage.

The crowd presses against the barriers.

Nora searches for another route.

Her eyes dart from one alley to the next.

She calculates.

She panics.

**"No... no, no, no..."**

In the distance, the metal door to the galleries closes.

The sound is tiny.

Almost nothing.

But you understand immediately.

You're too late.

The mother you helped vanishes into the crowd with her living child in her arms.

You should feel relief.

You do.

But not only that.

Nora grabs your hand.

**"There may still be a way in through the cellars."**

She's lying.

You know it.

She knows it too.

But she refuses to let go yet.

choices.text: Look for a way out with Nora anyway

fin_humaine.title: Ending — A Life Saved
fin_humaine.text:
You find no other way in.

Nora pounds on a locked door until her hands bleed.

**"Open up!"**

No one answers.

The city shakes.

The sirens twist in the air.

You think of the child.

Of his arms around his mother's neck.

Of that tiny life that goes on somewhere because you lost a few minutes.

Nora collapses against you.

**"You see?"** she murmurs. **"You see why I wanted to choose in your place?"**

You don't answer.

There is nothing to answer.

The light reaches the end of the street.

White.

Enormous.

Nora squeezes your hand.

This time, she doesn't pull you.

She stays.

And in the final seconds, you understand something both horrible and gentle:

you didn't save the world.

You didn't survive.

But somewhere, a child is still breathing.

fin_humaine_douce.title: Ending — No Longer Running
fin_humaine_douce.narrator: Sometimes the last freedom is to stop running.
fin_humaine_douce.text:
You take Nora's hand.

**"Stop."**

She shakes her head.

**"No. There has to be another route. There's always another route."**

**"Nora."**

Your calm disarms her more surely than a shout.

She understands.

The door is closed.

The shelter is too far.

The world won't wait any longer.

She rests her forehead against your shoulder.

**"I tried."**

**"I know."**

Around you, the city seems almost silent.

Far off, a mother runs with her child in her arms.

You don't know whether they'll reach a shelter.

But they're running.

They have a chance.

Nora follows your gaze.

She cries.

Not only because she's losing you.

Because she finally understands why you would have chosen the world.

The light arrives.

You close your eyes.

Her hand stays in yours.

aider_cafe_suite.title: Those Who Stay
aider_cafe_suite.narrator: When the world collapses, some gestures become bigger than the people who make them.
aider_cafe_suite.text:
You stay.

The waitress is still trembling.

The old bookseller doesn't understand how to reach the shelter.

A child searches for his mother among the overturned tables.

Nora looks at you.

**"We have to leave."**

You know she's right.

But you see the shaking hands.

The empty faces.

The people who didn't understand fast enough.

So you help.

You give directions.
You move a cabinet that fell in front of the exit.
You carry the bookseller to the sidewalk.

Nora ends up helping too.

Not because she wants to.

Because she loves you enough to hate what you're doing.

When you finally get outside, the street has changed.

The route to the hospital is cut off.

choices.text: Try again to reach the shelter
Help the last ones down into a cellar
Stay where you are without knowing what to do

fin_cafe.title: Ending — The Café of the Last Seconds
fin_cafe.narrator: Not every shelter is deep enough to save a body. Some only save what is left of our humanity.
fin_cafe.text:
The shelter is too far.

Nora knows it before you do.

She looks at the street.

Then at the café.

Then at you.

**"You gave us our time."**

It isn't a reproach.

Not entirely.

Inside, the waitress is still breathing.

The bookseller clutches his old radio to his chest.

The child has found his mother.

You didn't save the city.

You didn't reach the shelter.

But around you, several people are alive a few minutes longer because you didn't know how to leave.

The radio crackles.

An old song plays between emergency messages.

Nora sits beside you, behind the overturned counter.

**"I wish I'd been selfish enough to save you."**

You answer her:

**"You were."**

She smiles through her tears.

Outside, the light rises.

fin_cave.title: Ending — The Cellar
fin_cave.narrator: We don't always choose to survive. Sometimes we only choose where to wait for the end.
fin_cave.text:
You help the last ones down into the café's cellar.

It isn't a real shelter.

Just thick walls.
Dusty bottles.
A flickering bulb.

Nora shuts the door behind you.

She no longer says there's still a chance.

You're glad she has stopped lying.

The waitress holds the child tight.

The bookseller opens his book of poetry.

His voice trembles, but he reads anyway.

No one really understands the verses.

It doesn't matter.

For a few seconds, there's a room full of people listening together.

Nora takes your hand in the dark.

**"That's why I wanted to keep you alive."**

**"For what?"**

**"So the world keeps someone like you."**

The cellar shakes.

The light goes out.

triage_retard.title: The Last Civilian
triage_retard.narrator: In wanting no one left outside, you can end up on the wrong side yourself.
triage_retard.text:
You keep going.

One more person.

Then another.

Nora calls for you.

The doctor does too.

But an injured teenage girl can't walk.

You carry her to the door.

She gets through.

The door begins to close.

Nora screams your name.

You run.

Too late.

The armored door seals between you.

On the other side, Nora pounds.

Again.

Again.

The doctor shouts something you can't hear.

Protocol S-12 will not be launched.

You're on the wrong side.

But the teenage girl is inside.

And several others with her.

choices.text: Place your hand on the door

fin_derriere_porte.title: Ending — Behind the Door
fin_derriere_porte.narrator: A closed door can save lives on both sides, but not in the same way.
fin_derriere_porte.text:
You place your hand on the armored door.

On the other side, Nora is surely placing hers.

You can't see her.

You can't hear her.

But you know her.

You imagine her rage.
Her fear.
Her way of still refusing reality.

The automated voice announces full sealing.

Then silence.

Protocol S-12 will not save the world.

But the civilians you brought in may live.

The teenage girl.
The waitress.
The children.
The old man.

A few lives.

Not enough for the history books.

Enough that your choice isn't empty.

When the light arrives, you keep your hand against the door.

So that Nora knows, on the other side, that you were still there.

tramway_matin.title: The Morning Tram
tramway_matin.narrator: Ordinary days are full of details we believe will last forever.
tramway_matin.text:
The tram screeches around the bends.

A woman sleeps against the window.
A student skims a textbook without really reading it.
Someone is listening to music far too loud.

Your phone buzzes again.

Nora:

> If you're still late, I'm drinking your coffee too.

An old ad plays on the screens in the car.

> VISIT THE HISTORIC SHELTERS OF SAINT-ORIEL

No one looks up.

The driver announces an unusual slowdown near the military district.

Then the routine resumes.

As if the world were still hesitating.

souvenir_nora.title: The Blue Bench
souvenir_nora.narrator: We grow attached to people long before we understand we love them.
souvenir_nora.text:
As you step off the tram, you pass an old blue bench.

Nora always calls it "the depressing bench" because it faces a parking lot.

You remember a winter evening.

She had waited for you here for two hours after your car accident.

When you asked her why she stayed out in the cold, she said:

**"Because someone had to be there when you woke up."**

You laughed.

She didn't.

Even today, you're not sure that sentence was a joke.

choices.text: Send Nora a photo of the bench

fete_foraine.title: The Closed Funfair
fete_foraine.narrator: Abandoned places often look like memories that refuse to die.
fete_foraine.text:
The old funfair has been closed for years.

Still, Nora always insists on walking past it.

The big wheel creaks in the wind.

Dead lights still hang beneath the stalls.

Nora points at a rusty shooting gallery.

**"Remember when you tried to win that hideous plush?"**

What you remember most is that she kept it.

She notices your look.

**"It's still at my place."**

Then she adds, more gently:

**"I keep a lot of useless things."**

choices.text: Ask her why she kept it

confidence_legere.title: Useless Things
confidence_legere.narrator: People rarely talk directly about love. They talk about the objects they never threw away.
confidence_legere.text:
Nora shrugs.

**"I don't know. I like keeping things that remind me some days really existed."**

She looks at the river.

The wind lifts her hair.

For a second, she seems tired.

Not physically.

Like someone who already knows something is about to be taken from her.

Then she finds her smile again.

**"Anyway. If the world ends today, at least the plush might survive."**

You laugh.

In the distance, a very faint siren sounds.

Too far away to worry anyone.

choices.text: Ask her why she says that

station_metro.title: The Flooded Station
station_metro.narrator: Panicked crowds look like waves that have forgotten where they were going.
station_metro.text:
The metro station is overflowing.

Families rush down the stairs.

An agent keeps trying to give directions over a crackling loudspeaker.

Nora moves fast.

Too fast.

Like someone who already knows the exact timing.

On a platform, a musician keeps playing the violin.

No one listens.

Then the power cuts out for a second.

Darkness swallows everything.

When the lights return, several people are already crying.

choices.text: Help an elderly woman who has fallen

metro_aide.title: Under the Neon
metro_aide.narrator: Even at the edge of the end, some people still stop to offer a hand.
metro_aide.text:
You help the elderly woman to her feet.

She grips your sleeve as if you were the last stable thing in the world.

Nora comes back to you through the crowd.

She looks furious.

Then she sees the woman trembling.

So she helps too.

That contradiction again.

The way she wants to save everyone except when it comes to you.

Far off, a rumble makes the rails vibrate.

Not a train.

Something much farther away.

And much bigger.

message_banc.title: The Message
message_banc.narrator: Some conversations already feel like memories before they are even over.
message_banc.text:
You send Nora the photo of the bench.

Three little dots appear almost immediately.

Nora:

> Oh no.
> The depressing bench.
> Are you trying to make me nostalgic first thing in the morning?

You keep walking.

Nora sends a second photo.

The old plush from the funfair.

Still sitting on a shelf at her place.

> I told you I keep useless things.

Then:

> Hurry up anyway.
> The coffee is getting cold.

For a few seconds, the world still looks exactly as it did yesterday.

marche_couverte.title: The Covered Market
marche_couverte.narrator: The most ordinary places become sacred once they are gone.
marche_couverte.text:
Crossing the covered market, Nora stops in front of a fruit seller.

She hesitates for a long time before buying a peach.

**"It's ridiculous what they charge now."**

Then she cuts it in half with the little knife from her pocket.

She hands you half.

It tastes impossibly normal.

Around you, people talk about the weather, work, football.

A screen hanging overhead shows political debates with the sound off.

Nora watches the pictures.

Then she looks away at once.

Like someone trying to forget something she already knows.

choices.text: Ask her if something is bothering her
Pass by the old record shop

pharmacie.title: The Pharmacy
pharmacie.narrator: People quickly become their true selves when they think time is running out.
pharmacie.text:
A pharmacy is under siege.

People are screaming.

Some try to grab medicine.
Others are only looking for water.

A woman begs for insulin.

Nora slows down.

You see the conflict in her eyes immediately.

Leave.
Or help again.

The pharmacist finally throws boxes over the counter to calm the crowd.

Someone weeps behind you.

Someone laughs nervously.

The world is already starting to crack into pieces that don't fit together.

choices.text: Help the woman get her medication

famille_nora.title: Nora's Family
famille_nora.narrator: People rarely talk about their families when they are afraid of losing them.
famille_nora.text:
Nora is silent for a few seconds.

Then she sighs.

**"My mother still thinks I'll end up a history teacher."**

She smiles faintly.

**"She hates my current job. She says government labs smell of secrets and migraines."**

You laugh.

Nora looks at the rain behind the window.

**"My father collected old radios. When I was little, he'd sometimes wake me up at night just to listen to strange frequencies from the other side of the world."**

She lowers her eyes.

**"I think that's when I started being afraid of sirens."**

For a moment, she seems about to add something.

Then she thinks better of it.

radio_enfance.title: Nora's Father's Radios
radio_enfance.narrator: Childhood memories sometimes turn into warnings we understand too late.
radio_enfance.text:
Nora slowly stirs her spoon.

**"My father always said people think the end of the world would make a huge noise."**

She smiles sadly.

**"But according to him, the worst moment would be just before. When everything keeps going normally while someone, somewhere, already knows."**

You ask whether she thinks about that often.

She hesitates.

**"For a few weeks now? Yes."**

Silence falls.

In the café, someone drops coins.

A couple laughs by the window.

The coffee machine rumbles.

The world carries on.

A little longer.

nora_fissure_avant.title: Almost a Confession
nora_fissure_avant.narrator: Some secrets begin with an interrupted sentence.
nora_fissure_avant.text:
Nora opens her mouth.

**"If something really happened..."**

She stops.

You wait.

Her phone buzzes.

She looks at it.

Her face pales for a split second.

Then she locks the screen at once.

**"Nothing. Forget it."**

But now you notice she keeps checking the time every thirty seconds.

Like someone waiting for an invisible impact.

disquaire.title: The Record Shop
disquaire.narrator: Songs often last longer than the cities that play them.
disquaire.text:
Nora stops in front of an old record shop.

The shop is playing an old song out into the street.

She smiles at once.

**"My brother adored this band."**

You've never heard her talk about her brother.

She notices your expression.

**"He moved north years ago. We almost never talk."**

Then she adds:

**"We always think we'll have time later."**

The shopkeeper changes the record.

The song cuts off abruptly.

The silence suddenly feels strange.

choices.text: Ask her if she regrets it

regrets_nora.title: Things Put Off
regrets_nora.narrator: Regret often feels like a conversation you thought you would have tomorrow.
regrets_nora.text:
Nora keeps her eyes on the shop window.

**"Yes."**

No joke this time.

**"I spent so much time believing people would stay. My family. My friends. You."**

She laughs nervously.

**"It's stupid, right? As if the world owed us time."**

An ambulance passes in the distance.

Too fast.

Too early in the day.

Nora follows it with her eyes until it disappears.

Then she murmurs:

**"If something happened today, I think I'd mostly regret everything I never said."**

choices.text: Ask her what she never said
Tell her you still have time together

presque_amour.title: Something Important
presque_amour.narrator: Important words rarely make it all the way to the end.
presque_amour.text:
Nora looks at you.

Really looks.

As if she's trying to memorize your face.

**"I think I should have told you..."**

A siren sounds in the distance.

Not the alert yet.

Just an ambulance.

But it's enough to make her stop.

She looks away.

**"Nothing."**

Then she starts walking faster again.

Like someone running from a sentence.
